entries.text: Lin selected the tape deck. The microphone lamp went dark, leaving the old reel turning slowly.
Thank you. Not because it's my voice, but because it kept this place alive for thirteen more years.
Don't trim it. Send the breath at the start too. Whoever hears the archive should know how nervous you were.
All right. Levels set, window connected. When the needle crosses the white line, I start the reel.
The reel quickened. Old tape hiss filled the room, then the transmission relay caught it softly.
“This is Cape Hill Community Radio. Good morning. May someone hear you today.”
When the receive lamp steadied, they climbed the narrow stairs to the roof. The eastern clouds had begun to pale.
So the last place we hear those words is up here. The wind is more honest than a monitor speaker.
Ten seconds to the master switch. Watch the status lamp; I'll cut the power.
An antenna cable swayed in the wind, keeping time for a voice that had already ended.
Did the archive send a receipt? I want to know it didn't remain only in our ears.
Received: old station call, six point eight seconds complete, marked as the final live record.
That's enough. When someone opens it, the first thing they hear will be your younger breath.
Zhou pressed the master switch. The status lamp died, and the city below entered morning in silence.
